name: USS Clemson
shortDescription: Early torpedo boat with massive per-hit torpedo damage, let down by detection worse than most tier III destroyer peers.

torpedoMounts.note: All four mounts traverse a full 180°, none are locked to one side.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 5s action, 40s cooldown, one of the fastest resets you'll see at this tier.

consumables.name: Smoke Generator
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 30s to lay, roughly 112s screen off a 160s cooldown. Built to park a team inside, not to dash through.

strengths: Twelve torpedo tubes across four mounts, enormous per-hit damage for tier III
Fast turret traverse and rudder shift keep her responsive even though the guns are a last resort
35.5-knot top speed lets her open the range or reposition after a torpedo run
weaknesses: No real armor, a couple of cruiser salvos will end you
Gun DPM is weak next to other tier III destroyers
6.5 km sea detection is worse than most other tier III destroyers, she's often spotted before she can spot back
Short torpedo range forces you in close, often inside your own detection range
tips: Don't start a gunfight on purpose. Your guns finish off a low-health target, they don't win fights.
Assume you'll be seen first. Lean on the Smoke Generator to approach or disengage rather than natural concealment.
Save the smoke for setting up a torpedo run or breaking contact. It's too valuable this early to burn on damage farming alone.

threats.reason: One HE salvo can end you, and their guns outrange yours.
Most tier III destroyers see her before she sees them, so she rarely gets to dictate the engagement.

summary: Huge per-hit torpedo damage for the tier, though concealment is below average, not the asset it's often assumed to be.
A torpedo boat first, guns are strictly a last resort.
Paper-thin. One good salvo ends the game.
playstyle.detail: Clemson isn't built to win a fight in the open, and despite the torpedo-boat reputation she isn't especially good at staying hidden either. Her detection range runs worse than most tier III peers, so the smoke generator is doing the work natural concealment doesn't. Pop smoke, line up the angle, and let the torpedoes make your case for you. The instant someone spots you back, the plan has already gone sideways, so don't wait around to find out how badly.

imageCredit: USS Clemson (DD-186) steaming at high speed, c. 1919. Naval History and Heritage Command, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

goalTags.note: Four triple mounts, twelve tubes total. Very few ships this early can put that much ordnance in the water at once.
